info.title: NVIDIA Kubernetes Engine (NVKE) API
info.description:
The NVKE REST API manages Kubernetes clusters, control planes, node pools and
nodes on NVIDIA Infra Controller (NICo) infrastructure. It is used by
Operators who run NVKE on their own infrastructure, by their automation, and
by the `nvkectl` CLI.

**Release:** Alpha (public preview). Examples are illustrative: IDs,
timestamps and names are placeholders.

## Conventions

**Base URL and content type.** All operations are served under `/api`.
Request and response bodies are `application/json`.

**Authentication.** Every operation requires an HTTP bearer token (JWT) in
the `Authorization` header. The Operator configures which token issuers the
management plane trusts and which identities are admitted. Tokens must be
signed with an asymmetric algorithm by a configured issuer, carry `exp` and
`sub`, and match a configured audience. Admission rules are defined per
issuer and match either Kubernetes service accounts or SPIFFE IDs.

| Status | Returned when |
|---|---|
| 401 | No token, unknown issuer, invalid signature, expired token, or wrong audience. The response includes a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` header. |
| 403 | The token is valid but its subject matches no admission rule. |

`nvkectl` obtains a short-lived token automatically when run against a
management cluster.

**Errors.** Error responses use a single body shape:
`{ "message": "A cluster already exists with the name \"tenant-a-prod\"" }`

| Status | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 400 | The request failed validation. This includes malformed path or query parameters (for example, a non-UUID ID), duplicate names, and the rule violations listed under each operation. |
| 401 / 403 | Authentication or admission failure, see above. |
| 404 | The resource does not exist. No body is returned. |
| 409 | The request conflicts with an operation already in progress, or with the parent resource's state. |
| 500 | Unexpected server error. The body carries a message. |

**Asynchronous operations.** Create operations return 201 with the persisted
object immediately; provisioning continues in the background. Delete
operations return 202 and set the resource's `deleting` condition. Track
progress by polling the resource and reading its conditions. There is no
separate operation resource or callback.

**Update (PATCH) semantics.** PATCH operations use a field-level merge. They
do not follow RFC 7386 JSON Merge Patch.

| Value sent | Effect |
|---|---|
| Field omitted | Unchanged. |
| `null` | Rejected with 400. No field is nullable, and `null` does not clear a value. |
| `""` (empty string) | Stored as empty for `description` and `systemReservedMemory`. For `kubeReservedMemory`, restores the default. Rejected for `nico.release`. |
| `[]` (empty array) | Clears the list. UUID arrays are de-duplicated. |
| `nico` sub-object | Merged field by field, not replaced. |

Unknown fields in a PATCH body are rejected with 400.

**Lists.** List operations return all matching results in a single response.
Pagination and ordering are not supported in this release. Filters are exact
match. Unrecognized query parameters are ignored.

## Unauthenticated endpoints

The following are served without a token and are outside the `/api`
resource model.

| Path | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `GET /openapi.yaml` | The OpenAPI 3.0 specification for this API. |
| `GET /api/docs/` | Interactive API documentation (Swagger UI). |
| `GET /healthz` | Liveness. Returns `{"status":"ok"}`. |
| `GET /readyz` | Readiness, including dependency checks. Returns 503 when a dependency is unavailable. |

## Identity

Every resource has a server-assigned UUID `id`, which is used in paths.
Cluster names are unique per management plane; node pool names are unique
within a cluster. Cluster kubeconfigs are retrieved with `nvkectl`, not
through this API.

tags.name: Clusters
tags.description:
A Kubernetes cluster. Holds the Kubernetes version, network, CNI, etcd
encryption, control-plane configuration and conditions.

**Infrastructure provider.** Each cluster, control plane and node pool
carries exactly one provider object. `nico` runs the cluster on NVIDIA
Infra Controller (NICo) bare-metal infrastructure: organization, site
and VPC at the cluster level; instance type, networking, SSH key groups
and release at the control-plane and node pool level. `launchLayer`
runs it on LaunchLayer compute: VPC or organization, site and security
groups at the cluster level; instance type and host OS or VM profile at
the control-plane and node pool level. A deployment accepts only the
providers its operator enables (`supportedInfraProviders`, NICo by
default) and rejects any other with 400. A cluster's provider is fixed
at creation.

**Kubernetes versions.** Versions are semantic-version cores (X.Y.Z) with
no leading `v`. Control-plane upgrades move forward one minor version at a
time; downgrades and major-version changes are rejected. Worker node pools
may trail the control plane by at most 3 minor versions. A new node pool
starts at the cluster's Kubernetes version. `controlPlaneKubernetesVersion`
and a pool's `kubernetesVersion` are desired versions; the control plane's
current running version is reported in `ControlPlaneStatus.kubernetesVersion`.

**Networking.** New clusters use ovn-kubernetes (default version 2.4.2).
Calico is retained only for existing fleets and its creation path is
disabled by default. Pod and service CIDRs are IPv4,
private, and immutable after
creation; the defaults are 192.168.0.0/16 for pods and 10.96.0.0/12 for
services. NVKE allocates a /24 from the pod CIDR to each node, so the pod
CIDR must have room for every desired node plus surge, or one spare block
when surge is 0. This is checked when clusters and node pools are created
or scaled. Set `controlPlaneVIP` to use a virtual IP (kube-vip) as the API
server endpoint; when omitted, the first control-plane node's IP is the
endpoint. The VIP must not fall inside the pod or service CIDR.

tags.name: Control plane
tags.description:
NVKE manages each cluster's control plane through a dedicated control-plane
controller. You declare the control plane once, in `controlPlaneConfig`,
and NVKE provisions, upgrades and replaces control-plane nodes to match it.
Node pools always contain worker nodes.

- **Size.** `controlPlaneConfig.desiredCount` sets the number of
  control-plane nodes. It is required when you create a cluster.
- **Rollouts.** When the control-plane configuration changes (release
  or Kubernetes version), NVKE compares each control-plane node with the
  desired configuration and replaces drifted nodes. `maxSurge` (0 or 1)
  controls whether a replacement node is added before the old one is
  removed. Progress is reported in `ControlPlaneStatus.rollout` and, per
  node, in `Node.controlPlaneRollout`.
- **Recycling gate.** When `enableCPNodeRecycling` is false, drifted nodes
  are detected and reported as pending but are not replaced until an
  operator acts.
- **Deletes.** Control-plane node deletes are serialized. A delete request
  is recorded first (`deleteRequested`) and NVKE starts teardowns one at a
  time. A delete is rejected if it would leave fewer than 3 healthy, joined
  control-plane nodes.

The control plane is read at `GET /clusters/{clusterID}/control-plane` and
changed through `PATCH /clusters/{clusterID}`. Its configuration history is
an ordered list of snapshots of control-plane configuration changes.

**Releases (`release`).** The OS and first-boot configuration for
every node come from a release the Operator supplies to the management
plane. Control-plane and node pool requests select them by name in
`nico.release`. Changing `release` on a node pool or on the control
plane triggers a rollout of the affected nodes to the new release.

tags.name: Node pools
tags.description:
A group of worker nodes sharing an instance type, release and
Kubernetes version. Node pool names are unique within a cluster. The
configuration history of a node pool is an ordered list of snapshots of
its configuration changes.

tags.name: Node sets
tags.description:
A read-only, immutable snapshot of a node pool's configuration at a point
in time. `NodePool.currentNodeSetID` identifies the active one.

tags.name: Nodes
tags.description:
A single machine in a cluster, in a node pool or in the control plane,
with lifecycle and health conditions.

get.description: Returns all clusters, or the cluster whose name matches `name`.

post.description:
Creates a cluster and starts provisioning. The cluster is returned before
provisioning completes.

Returns 400 for, among others: a duplicate cluster name; missing
`nico.orgID`, `siteID` or `vpcID`; an unsupported `cniPlugin`; a
missing `controlPlaneConfig.nico.release`; a
control-plane `maxSurge` greater than 1; a pod CIDR too small for the
requested nodes plus surge; a `controlPlaneVIP` inside the pod or
service CIDR.

get.description:
Returns one cluster. Once provisioning finishes, `conditions.provisioning`
is False and `conditions.provisioned` is True.

404.description: Cluster not found. No body is returned.

patch.description:
All fields are optional. See the API description for merge rules.

Returns 400 for, among others: a Kubernetes downgrade, major-version
change, or a jump of more than one minor version; an upgrade that would
leave a worker pool more than 3 minor versions behind;
`enableEtcdEncryption: false` or `enableOidc: false`; combining OIDC or
etcd enablement with a version upgrade; etcd or OIDC enablement on a
cluster that is not provisioned or is deleting; any `network` value;
a control-plane `maxSurge` greater than 1.

Returns 409 when another mutually exclusive cluster operation is in
progress (`etcd_encryption`, `etcd_key_rotation`, `k8s_upgrade`,
`cp_nodes_recycling`, `oidc_enable`, `certificate_renewal`), or the
control plane is upgrading or recycling nodes. A failed certificate
renewal can retain the lock until an operator clears it; see the
retained-lock recovery procedure in
controller/docs/certificate-renewal.md. A rotation that fails after
`prepare` keeps the `etcd_key_rotation` lock until its workflow is
reset and completes; see
controller/docs/etcd-encryption-key-rotation.md#phase-aware-recovery.

controlPlaneChange.summary: Resize the control plane and move it to a new release

404.description: Cluster not found. No body is returned.

409.description:
Another mutually exclusive cluster operation is in progress. The
message names the operation (etcd_encryption, etcd_key_rotation,
k8s_upgrade, cp_nodes_recycling, oidc_enable, certificate_renewal).
A failed certificate renewal can retain the lock until an operator
clears it; see the retained-lock recovery procedure in
controller/docs/certificate-renewal.md. A rotation that fails after
prepare keeps the etcd_key_rotation lock until its workflow is reset
and completes; see
controller/docs/etcd-encryption-key-rotation.md#phase-aware-recovery.

delete.description:
Starts deletion and sets `conditions.deleting` to `True`. A cluster can
be deleted in any state, including while it is provisioning or
upgrading. Deletion takes precedence over an in-progress or retained
etcd encryption, etcd key rotation or certificate renewal.

404.description: Cluster not found. No body is returned.

get.description:
Read-only view of the control plane: the persisted configuration plus
aggregate runtime status (node counts, current Kubernetes version,
rollout progress, and upgrade and recycling conditions). Change the
control plane through `PATCH /clusters/{clusterID}`.

404.description: Cluster not found. No body is returned.

get.description:
Returns the control-plane configuration change history, oldest first.
Each entry shows which rollout-relevant fields changed relative to the
previous snapshot. Use it to resolve the `pinnedConfigurationID` on each
control-plane node and the cluster's desired `configurationId`.

404.description: Cluster not found. No body is returned.

get.summary: Get the SPIRE server the cluster's nodes point at
get.description:
Returns the SPIRE server last requested through
`PATCH /clusters/{clusterID}/spire-server`, and for each node the
server its SPIRE agent points at and whether the agent holds a valid
X.509 SVID from it. Node status is read live from each node agent on
every call; an unreachable node is reported with `reachable: false`.

200.description: Requested server and live per-node SPIRE agent status

404.description: Cluster not found. No body is returned.

patch.summary: Point the cluster's nodes at a SPIRE server
patch.description:
Starts a `spire_server_update` operation that points the SPIRE agent on
every node of the cluster at the given server and waits for each agent
to hold an SVID from it. Track it through `conditions.updateInProgress`
and `conditions.updateFailed` on the cluster, and per node through
`GET /clusters/{clusterID}/spire-server`. Repeating the request with
the same server is safe, including while it is in progress.

requestBody.description: The SPIRE server the cluster's nodes should point at.

404.description: Cluster not found. No body is returned.

409.description:
Another cluster operation is in progress, or a SPIRE server update
to a different server is in progress. The message names the
operation.

Creates a worker node pool and starts provisioning. The pool takes the
cluster's Kubernetes version.

patch.description:
All fields are optional. Changes to the Kubernetes version, release
or other node configuration create a new NodeSet and roll the pool's
nodes to it.

Returns 400 for, among others: sending a field that is fixed at
creation (for example `instanceTypeID`); `nico.release: ""`; any update
to a control-plane node pool, which is configured through the cluster's
`controlPlaneConfig` instead. That last refusal does not depend on the
control-plane mutation lock, so retrying later does not help.

delete.description:
Deletes a node pool from a running cluster. Also returns 202, with no
further effect, if the pool or its cluster is already being deleted.

Returns 409 for a control-plane node pool while etcd encryption, etcd key
rotation or certificate renewal holds the control-plane mutation lock.
Retry once the operation has finished. A failed certificate renewal can
retain the lock until an operator clears it; see the retained-lock
recovery procedure in controller/docs/certificate-renewal.md.
A rotation that fails after `prepare` keeps the `etcd_key_rotation` lock
until its workflow is reset and completes; see
controller/docs/etcd-encryption-key-rotation.md#phase-aware-recovery.

404.description: Node pool not found. No body is returned.

A control-plane node pool cannot be deleted while etcd encryption, etcd
key rotation or certificate renewal holds the control-plane mutation

parameters.description: `true` returns only control-plane nodes; `false` only workers

get.description:
Returns one node. Control-plane nodes do not belong to a node pool, so
their `nodePoolID` and `nodeSetID` are the nil UUID. `nico` is omitted
when none of its fields are set.

404.description: Node not found. No body is returned.

delete.description:
Deletes a single node from a running cluster. Include a
`machineHealthIssue` to flag the underlying machine for repair.

For control-plane nodes, a delete sets `deleteRequested`; NVKE then
starts teardowns one node at a time. `forceUnreachable` is applied
automatically when the node is unhealthy.

Also returns 202, with no further effect, if the node, pool or cluster
is already being deleted or a delete is already requested.

Returns 400 when deletion would leave no joined control-plane node or
`machineHealthIssue` is invalid. Delete the cluster to remove its last
joined control-plane node.
Deleting a control-plane node requires controlPlaneVIP because the controller
replaces it, unless allowControlPlaneWithoutVIP is enabled for development.
Worker node deletion is unaffected.

Returns 409 for a control-plane node while etcd encryption, etcd key
rotation or certificate renewal holds the control-plane mutation lock.
Retry once the operation has finished. A failed certificate renewal can
retain the lock until an operator clears it; see the retained-lock
recovery procedure in controller/docs/certificate-renewal.md.
A rotation that fails after `prepare` keeps the `etcd_key_rotation` lock
until its workflow is reset and completes; see
controller/docs/etcd-encryption-key-rotation.md#phase-aware-recovery.

Lists the config profiles available to the management plane.

Unauthorized.description: No valid bearer token was presented.

Forbidden.description: The token verified, but its subject matches no admission rule.

bearerAuth.description:
A JWT from an issuer the Operator has configured, carried as `Authorization:
Bearer <token>`.

CreateClusterRequest.description:
A cluster and, optionally, its initial node pools. The provider payload is
fixed at creation.

name.description: Cluster name. Lowercase DNS label, unique per management plane. Node names are derived from it.

controlPlaneKubernetesVersion.description: Kubernetes version for the cluster, as X.Y.Z with no leading "v".

cniPlugin.description: CNI plugin. Defaults to ovn-kubernetes when omitted. calico is a disabled-by-default legacy override.

cniVersion.description: CNI version, as X.Y.Z. Defaults to 3.30.1 for legacy calico or 2.4.2 for ovn-kubernetes.

etcdEncrypted.description: Encrypt etcd at rest. Can be turned on later with `enableEtcdEncryption`; cannot be turned off.

controlPlaneVIP.description:
Virtual IP for the API server through kube-vip. Omit to skip kube-vip and
use the first control-plane node's IP as the API server endpoint. Must not
fall inside the pod or service CIDR. An explicit empty string is rejected.
By default, a cluster without a VIP must have exactly one desired
control-plane node. Scale-up above one node, upgrades and node replacement
require a VIP unless the controller deployment enables the development-only
allowControlPlaneWithoutVIP setting. That override keeps the initializing
node's IP as the endpoint; replacing that node can break API access.
Quorum, health and deletion protections still apply.

teleportEnabled.description: Enable Teleport SSH enrollment for nodes in this cluster. When omitted, the server-side default for the site is applied.

version.description: Exact agent release version. An empty value disables agent convergence.

NodeAgentUpgradeStatus.description: The active agent upgrade and latest retry error.

nodeId.description: ID of the selected control-plane node.

targetVersion.description: Exact version accepted for this upgrade.

method.description: Installation method from the controller configuration.

phase.description: Pending before installation starts. Running includes retries.

errorMessage.description: Latest failure message while retries continue.

ControlPlaneConfig.description: The control-plane configuration in effect, including the desired node-agent version.

configurationId.description: ID of the current configuration snapshot.

desiredCount.description: The desired number of cluster-level control plane nodes. Creating a cluster with or increasing this count above 1 requires controlPlaneVIP on the cluster unless the development-only allowControlPlaneWithoutVIP setting is enabled.

maxSurge.description: Extra control-plane nodes allowed during a rollout (0 or 1).

autoScaleDownDisabled.description: When true, automatic control-plane scale-down is disabled, so decreasing desiredCount leaves the surplus nodes in place. When scale-down is enabled it never reduces the control plane below the fault-tolerant floor of three nodes.

nodeRebalanceDisabled.description: When true, steady-state control-plane instance-type rebalancing is disabled. When unset (the default) the controller surges a more-preferred replacement for a node on a less-preferred instance type and sheds the old node through the control-plane delete path, independent of autoScaleDownDisabled. Existing clusters are opted out at migration time.

provisioningMonitorDisabled.description: When true, nodes stuck in provisioning past the timeout are not replaced automatically.

systemReservedMemory.description: Memory reserved for system daemons. Nodes reserve 16Gi when omitted.

machineAnnotations.description: Annotations applied to control-plane CAPI Machines at creation, including scale-out and replacement Machines. Fixed at cluster creation and not reconciled after provisioning. Keys under nke.nvidia.com, nke.io, nvke.nvidia.com, kubernetes.io, k8s.io, cluster.x-k8s.io and their subdomains require an explicit deployment allowlist entry for this metadata type.

Keys under nke.nvidia.com, nke.io, nvke.nvidia.com, kubernetes.io, k8s.io, cluster.x-k8s.io and their subdomains require an explicit deployment allowlist entry for this metadata type.

nodeLabels.description: Labels applied to control-plane nodes, as a map of keys to values. Set at creation.

teleportEnabled.description: Whether Teleport SSH enrollment is enabled for control plane nodes.

Read-only view of a cluster's control plane: its persisted configuration

Changes to `release` or the Kubernetes version start a control-plane
rollout. All fields are optional. A provider payload that does not match the
cluster's provider is rejected with 400.
Rollout-triggering changes require controlPlaneVIP unless the development-only
allowControlPlaneWithoutVIP setting is enabled. maxSurge alone does not
trigger a rollout and remains mutable without a VIP.

desiredCount.description:
The desired number of cluster-level control plane nodes. Must be at least 1.
Increasing the count above 1 requires controlPlaneVIP on the cluster unless the development-only allowControlPlaneWithoutVIP setting is enabled.

maxSurge.description: Extra control-plane nodes allowed during a rollout (0 or 1).

autoScaleDownDisabled.description: When true, automatic control-plane scale-down is disabled, so decreasing desiredCount leaves the surplus nodes in place. When scale-down is enabled it never reduces the control plane below the fault-tolerant floor of three nodes.

nodeRebalanceDisabled.description: When true, steady-state control-plane instance-type rebalancing is disabled. When unset (the default) the controller surges a more-preferred replacement for a node on a less-preferred instance type and sheds the old node through the control-plane delete path, independent of autoScaleDownDisabled. Existing clusters are opted out at migration time.

provisioningMonitorDisabled.description: When true, nodes stuck in provisioning past the timeout are not replaced automatically.

teleportEnabled.description: Enable or disable Teleport SSH enrollment for control plane nodes.

Cluster.description:
A Kubernetes cluster. Holds the Kubernetes version, network, CNI, etcd
encryption, control-plane configuration and conditions.

controlPlaneKubernetesVersion.description: Desired control-plane Kubernetes version. The running version is in ControlPlaneStatus.

etcdEncrypted.description: Whether etcd is encrypted at rest.

enableCPNodeRecycling.description:
When true, control-plane upgrades and configuration changes replace nodes
automatically. When false, nodes needing replacement are reported as pending and
wait for an operator.

teleportEnabled.description: Whether Teleport SSH enrollment is enabled for nodes in this cluster.

nextCertRenewalDue.description:
The next scheduled certificate-renewal time. A value in the past is
overdue unless a certificate-renewal operation is currently accepted.
Unset until the controller first sees the cluster, which schedules
the first check one renewal interval later.

UpdateClusterRequest.description: Changes to a cluster. All fields are optional; unknown fields are rejected.

enableCPNodeRecycling.description: Turn automatic control-plane node replacement on or off.

controlPlaneKubernetesVersion.description:
Target control-plane version, as X.Y.Z with no leading "v". Must be newer than
the current version by at most one minor version and keep every worker pool
within 3 minor versions.
The cluster must have controlPlaneVIP configured unless the development-only
allowControlPlaneWithoutVIP setting is enabled.

teleportEnabled.description: Enable or disable Teleport SSH enrollment for nodes in this cluster.

enableEtcdEncryption.description:
`true` starts one-way etcd encryption on a provisioned cluster. `false` is
rejected. `true` on an already-encrypted cluster does nothing. Other updates
return 409 while it runs.

enableOidc.description:
`true` starts one-way OIDC authentication enablement. `false` is rejected.
Cannot be combined with a control-plane upgrade or etcd enablement. Other
updates return 409 while it runs.

network.description:
The cluster network cannot be changed after creation; any network value in an
update is rejected.

ClusterNetworkCreateConfig.description: Pod and service network. Immutable after creation. Defaults apply when omitted.

podCIDR.description:
Comma-separated IPv4 pod CIDRs. Each must be private, with a prefix length from

## nvkectl bootstrap site

Bootstrap a new NVKE management cluster from a site spec file

### Required options

`--sitespec`

### Synopsis

Bootstrap a vanilla Kubernetes cluster from the nodes described by the site
spec file passed with -f/--sitespec: pre-provisioned hosts it lists
(infra.provider provisioned, the default), or machines CAPNICo allocates from a
NICo site (infra.provider nico).

The site spec file is loaded and validated first. On any invalid or missing
field the command fails immediately with a clear error, before any workflow is
dispatched or any node is touched.

The bootstrap side-loads the images this repository builds, nke-controller:latest
and, with the provisioned provider, cluster-api-provider-provisioned:latest,
which "make -C cli images" builds. With nico, CAPNICo's image is public and
pulled by the cluster; --release pins it to an NVKR release's artifact. --nvke-controller-image and --provisioned-provider-image, or
NVKECTL_NVKE_CONTROLLER_IMAGE and NVKECTL_CAPI_PROVISIONED_IMAGE, name other images, such as
ones pushed to a registry; a flag wins over its variable. cli/README.md lists
every NVKECTL_* variable.

Every node becomes a control-plane node. Once the cluster is up, the
control-plane NoSchedule taint is removed from each node so workloads can run.

With nico, infra.nico names the NICo and the MachineImage and ClusterRelease
manifests the controller needs; the NICo token is read from the file the
NVKECTL_NICO_CREDENTIALS variable names; the login rendered into every node
comes from NVKECTL_NODE_USER and NVKECTL_NODE_PASSWORD; and
spire.externalAddress is required unless --disable-mtls is set. The nodes'
names and addresses are not printed; read them with "kubectl get nodes -o wide"
on the finished cluster.

See the bundled examples/sitespec.yaml and docs/sitespec.md for the
site spec file format.

```
nvkectl bootstrap site [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  # Validate and bootstrap from a site spec file
  nvkectl bootstrap site -f sitespec.yaml

  # Validate only — load, check, and print the site spec without dispatching
  nvkectl bootstrap site -f sitespec.yaml --dry-run

  # Deploy images you pushed to a registry instead of the local build
  nvkectl bootstrap site -f sitespec.yaml \
    --nvke-controller-image nvcr.io/<org>/nvke-controller:edge \
    --provisioned-provider-image nvcr.io/<org>/cluster-api-provider-provisioned:edge

  # Export this run's spans and log records to a collector the cluster can reach
  nvkectl bootstrap site -f sitespec.yaml --otlp-endpoint collector.example.com:4317
```

      --arch string                         Architecture of the release artifact to use, linux/amd64 or linux/arm64; default: the bootstrap host's, since the bootstrap CAPNICo runs in its Kind cluster. Only with --release.
      --diagnostics-dir string              Directory a failed bootstrap writes cluster diagnostics to before tearing the cluster down. With --verbose a successful bootstrap writes them too. Overrides NVKECTL_BOOTSTRAP_DIAGNOSTICS_DIR. (default "cluster-diagnostics")
      --disable-mtls                        Stand the site up without SPIFFE: no SPIRE, and the controller dials node agents in plaintext. The agents must be running with --disable-mtls too. Development only.

## nvkectl get providers

List infrastructure providers installed on the management cluster

### Aliases

`provider`

### Synopsis

List infrastructure providers installed on the management cluster.

This reads the site's Kubernetes cluster directly rather than the controller API, so it needs the kubeconfig registered with 'nvkectl config set-site --kubeconfig' and kubectl on PATH.

CONFIGURED means the provider's CRDs are established, its manager is available, and its credentials Secret exists. It does not mean those credentials work.

CREDENTIALS is the provider's own credential check, read from the NicoIdentity that names the provider's credentials Secret. nvkectl never runs a check: the provider checks every few minutes, and LAST CHECK is how long ago the latest check ran. A result is STALE when the provider's scheduled check is overdue or, if the provider publishes no usable schedule, when its last check, or its creation if it was never checked, is too old.

```
HEALTHY            the last check authenticated and read the current tenant
FAILING (reason)   the credentials are missing, invalid, rejected or forbidden
UNKNOWN (reason)   the check could not decide, for example during an outage
STALE              no check when one was due
PENDING            not checked yet
NO-IDENTITY        no NicoIdentity names the provider's credentials Secret
UNSUPPORTED        the provider does not serve NicoIdentity
UNREADABLE         nvkectl could not list NicoIdentities
-                  the provider has no credential health to report
```

HEALTHY does not prove that provisioning will succeed.

The set of providers listed is the set nvkectl knows how to describe. It is not a restriction: the controller accepts any infrastructure manifest written by hand.

## nvkectl patch cluster

Patch a tenant cluster

### Aliases

`clusters`

### Synopsis

Patch a tenant cluster on the management plane.

PATCH semantics apply: only the fields in the patch document are changed;
everything else on the cluster is left as it is. Pass the patch inline with
--patch, or from a file (or stdin via -) with --patch-file. Exactly one of
the two is required.

Example — bump the Kubernetes version:
```
nvkectl patch cluster my-cluster --patch 'controlPlaneKubernetesVersion: 1.31.0'
```

Example — patch file:
```
nvkectl patch cluster my-cluster --patch-file patch.yaml
```

Example — set the control-plane node count:
```
nvkectl patch cluster my-cluster --patch 'controlPlaneConfig: {desiredCount: 3}'
```

The patch document's fields must match the controller UpdateClusterRequest schema
exactly. See /api/docs on your management plane.

```
nvkectl patch cluster <name> [flags]
```

## nvkectl patch nodepool

Patch a node pool

### Aliases

`nodepools`

### Required options

`--cluster`

### Synopsis

Patch a node pool on the management plane.

Node pool names are unique within a cluster, so --cluster is required to
identify which pool to patch.

PATCH semantics apply: only the fields in the patch document are changed;
everything else on the node pool is left as it is. Pass the patch inline with
--patch, or from a file (or stdin via -) with --patch-file. Exactly one of
the two is required.

nvkectl can set desiredNodeCount so far. The API
accepts more, but anything else is rejected before the request is sent.

Example — scale a pool:
```
nvkectl patch nodepool gpu-workers --cluster my-cluster --patch 'desiredNodeCount: 8'
```

Example — patch file:
```
nvkectl patch nodepool gpu-workers --cluster my-cluster --patch-file patch.yaml
```

The patch document's fields must match the controller UpdateNodePoolRequest schema
exactly. See /api/docs on your management plane.

```

## nvkectl validate sitespec

Check a site spec the way nvkectl bootstrap site reads it

### Required options

`--sitespec`

### Synopsis

Check a site spec: every field is validated. With spire.upstreamCA: true,
NVKECTL_SPIRE_CA_CERT_FILE and NVKECTL_SPIRE_CA_KEY_FILE must both name
readable files; without it, they must be unset. The command prints "valid"
and exits 0 when the file is valid, and reports every problem otherwise. It
says so when spire.trustDomain is not set, since the bootstrap and the
controller stack install then both use the default.

With infra.provider nico, the bootstrap also reads what only its host holds:
the file NVKECTL_NICO_CREDENTIALS names, the files infra.nico names, the node
login in NVKECTL_NODE_USER and NVKECTL_NODE_PASSWORD, spire.externalAddress
(required unless --disable-mtls is given, as it is for "nvkectl bootstrap
site") and the https check on infra.nico.remote.endpoint. Those are reported
but do not fail the run, because the controller stack install runs this
command on a host that does not have them. --bootstrap-only fails on them, so
a file it passes is one "nvkectl bootstrap site" accepts on this host.

```
nvkectl validate sitespec [flags]
```

### Examples

```
  nvkectl validate sitespec -f sitespec.yaml
  nvkectl validate sitespec -f sitespec.yaml --bootstrap-only
  nvkectl validate sitespec -f sitespec.yaml --bootstrap-only --disable-mtls
```

### Options

```
      --allow-control-plane-without-vip   Permit a multi-node control plane without a VIP. Development only; bootstrap site needs the same flag.
      --bootstrap-only                    Also fail on what only the bootstrap host holds, as "bootstrap site" does
      --disable-mtls                      Check the file as "bootstrap site --disable-mtls" would: with infra.provider nico, spire.externalAddress is not required
  -h, --help                              help for sitespec
  -f, --sitespec string                   Path to the site spec (required)
```

      --site string   Override the active site for this invocation
  -v, --verbose       Enable debug logging
```
